nomad_overview.ov_assembling_body: The Flotilla is assembling across your ships. The first residents arrive in about %s.
nomad_overview.ov_assembling_note: You can interact with the Flotilla when it has assembled.
nomad_overview.ov_stores_detached_note: The Flotilla is detached; these holds are out of reach until it rejoins.
nomad_overview.ov_status_paused: PAUSED. The Flotilla has no flagship. The stores will not change, but production stops and residents leave at %s a month. Install the Nomad Flagship to resume.
nomad_overview.ov_status_detached: DETACHED. The Flotilla is detached.%s It consumes from its own stores (including the monthly supply of its ships) until it rejoins.
nomad_overview.ov_status_short_one: SHORT. %s is running short; efficiency is reduced until the shortage ends.
nomad_overview.ov_status_short_many: SHORT. %s are running short; efficiency is reduced until the shortage ends.
nomad_overview.ov_split_tip_body: Send every ship that carries a Nomad hullmod off as its own fleet, to hold position and defend themselves. It consumes from its own stores until you visit it to rejoin.
nomad_overview.ov_split_tip_upkeep: While detached its ships consume their monthly supply upkeep, %s supplies a month, from the Flotilla's own stores.
nomad_overview.ov_split_tip_officer_one: %s officer aboard would share the Flotilla's fate.
nomad_overview.ov_split_tip_officer_many: %s officers aboard would share the Flotilla's fate.
nomad_overview.ov_split_confirm_body: Send the Flotilla off on its own? It will hold position and defend itself, until you visit it to rejoin.
nomad_overview.ov_split_confirm_upkeep: Its ships will consume %s supplies a month from the Flotilla's own stores.
nomad_overview.ov_split_confirm_officer_one: %s officer aboard will share its fate if it is destroyed.
nomad_overview.ov_split_confirm_officer_many: %s officers aboard will share its fate if it is destroyed.
nomad_overview.ov_banner_subtitle: A migrant population living aboard your ships, with its own stores and production.
nomad_overview.ov_residents_tip_growth: The number of residents grows while every need is met and berths are free. A shortage or full berths stops growth; residents over the berth cap are lost.
nomad_overview.ov_residents_tip_migrants: Migrants join when you undock at an inhabited colony with free berths, at most once every six months per colony.
nomad_overview.ov_residents_tip_crew: You can also move crew across in the Stores list below: giving crew to the Flotilla is free and immediate; taking residents back out costs the crew price per person.
nomad_overview.ov_efficiency_tip_what: Multiplies every production allocation's output, Flotilla-wide. Works and colony items raise an allocation's yield, not global efficiency.
nomad_overview.ov_efficiency_tip_curve: Below 75%, the inputs of allocations scale with the outputs. Above 75%, inputs are fixed but outputs continue increasing. 75% represents the floor of minimum required material to make the output, but as you become more efficient you need fewer inputs for the same output.
nomad_overview.ov_efficiency_tip_staffing: Staffing shortage: %s jobs, %s residents needed to fill them. Global efficiency is affected by the unfilled fraction.
nomad_overview.ov_space_tip_stored: Currently stored: %s, taken from the pool below.
nomad_overview.ov_space_tip_overcap: Used space is greater than total space. Usually a ship left the fleet or a Nomad hullmod was removed. Nothing is removed now; allocations or stores are trimmed to fit at the next economy tick. Space held by Works, built or under construction, is freed only by scrapping or cancelling them.
nomad_overview.ov_space_tip_pool: Every non-resident store has one shared storage pool of %s: the free space, plus a small floor for each commodity, plus space from Bonded Hold if that is built. Only currently used stores draw from this pool (the sum of the Maximums can be higher than the storage pool).
nomad_overview.ov_space_tip_fill: The cap of each store is the lesser of its own Maximum storage and remaining free space (allocating space or building Works shrinks the free space).
nomad_overview.ov_space_tip_discard: Lowering a maximum below current stores discards the excess. It is not moved to your cargo.

nomad_allocations.al_balance_tip_what: Adds allocations until this allocation's net output is 0/mo, assuming its yield and the global efficiency stay the same.
nomad_allocations.al_balance_tip_sizing: It adjusts as if this commodity did not have a shortage if applicable. You may still need to fix the shortage yourself.
nomad_allocations.al_balance_tip_cost: Each allocation costs %s to build and has no refund if removed. Balancing stops at what your credits and free space allow, keeps enough free space for current storage, and never adds more jobs than the residents can staff.
nomad_allocations.al_balance_tip_headroom: Right now there is %s space to allocate, and the residents can staff %s more. Balance adds at most the smaller of the two.
nomad_allocations.al_balance_tip_input_short: An input is out of stock; there is nothing to balance against.
nomad_allocations.al_balance_tip_staff_cap: Every resident already has a job; no one is free to staff another allocation.
nomad_allocations.al_stepper_add_tip: Add space to this allocation. Each allocation added costs %s. Every add keeps enough free space for current storage. +max stops at what your credits and that reserve allow. You may allocate past what the residents can staff (unstaffed jobs decrease global efficiency).
nomad_allocations.al_stepper_remove_tip: Remove space from this allocation. No refunds.
nomad_allocations.al_balanceall_tip_what: Balances every producible allocation in turn, repeating until stable..
nomad_allocations.al_balanceall_tip_shortages: If you have multiple shortages, it may fail to balance or over-allocate. It never uses more than your free space, keeps enough of that for current storage, and never adds more jobs than the residents can staff.

nomad_allocations.al_balanceall_tip_headroom: Right now there is a maximum of %s possible space to allocate, and %s residents are idle.

nomad_manual.man_intro: The Flotilla is a population of migrants living aboard your ships. You will manage its stores and production from this screen. The Flotilla's population and stores are separate from your own cargo and crew.
nomad_manual.man_space_berths: A Nomad hullmod reduces a ship's cargo capacity and its maximum crew. The cargo it loses becomes {{Space}}, where the Flotilla stores goods and manages production. The maximum crew it loses becomes {{Berths}}, which limit how many residents can live in the Flotilla. A ship loses the cargo and crew wherever it is, but it adds Space and Berths to the Flotilla only while it is in the same fleet as the flagship.
nomad_manual.man_flagship: Installing the Nomad Flagship hullmod founds the Flotilla and opens this screen. The first residents take a few days to arrive. If the flagship is lost or put in storage, the Flotilla stops. It produces nothing, and its residents leave over time until there is another flagship.
nomad_manual.man_residents_growth: Residents staff the allocations and Works. The population grows slowly while every need is met and berths are free, and up to the berth cap. Migrants also join when you undock at an inhabited colony with berths available, at most once every six months from each colony. You can move crew to and from the Flotilla manually on the Overview tab.
nomad_manual.man_residents_needs: Every resident consumes Food, Supplies, Domestic Goods, and Luxury Goods each month, whether or not they are working. Each unit of allocated space consumes Heavy Machinery every month (it is not per-resident but instead per unit of allocated space).
nomad_manual.man_detaching: You can detach the Flotilla to allow it to travel as its own fleet. Detached, it keeps mining and defends itself if attacked, but it consumes only on its own stores and cannot exchange cargo or crew with your fleet. Its ships consume their monthly supplies from the Flotilla's stores while detached, at the same rate they cost your fleet. Bring your fleet to the detached Flotilla to rejoin.
nomad_manual.man_efficiency: Global efficiency is a single multiplier on how much the Flotilla produces. Below 75%, the inputs of allocations scale with the outputs. Above 75%, inputs are fixed but outputs continue increasing. 75% represents the floor of minimum required material to make the output, but as you become more efficient you need fewer inputs for the same output.
nomad_manual.man_efficiency_table:
For example, at these global efficiencies an allocation makes this much output for this much input:
    {{130%}}: {{1.3}} out for {{1}} in
    {{125%}}: {{1.25}} out for {{1}} in
    {{100%}}: {{1}} out for {{1}} in
    {{75%}}: {{0.75}} out for {{1}} in
    {{50%}}: {{0.5}} out for {{0.67}} in
nomad_manual.man_efficiency_staffing: The primary source of efficiency is staffing percentage: your working residents divided by the staff your allocations and Works need. If your staffing percentage is 50%, your global efficiency is halved.
nomad_manual.man_shortage: Another major factor for global efficiency is shortages. A shortage begins when you run out of a required store. Separate shortages will multiply together. Most shortages also cause population decreases (e.g. famines).
nomad_manual.man_yield: {{Yield}} is how much an allocation produces for each unit of Space. Every allocation starts at a base yield, which Works and colony items can raise. Yield scales output and input together, so at double yield an allocation makes twice as much and consumes twice the input. Global efficiency does not affect yield.
nomad_manual.man_production: Each allocation to Credits sells up to %s stored unit a month, at %s of base value. The most expensive good marked SELL on the stores list that is over %s of its effective cap is sold. Selling earns less than trading the goods yourself; it is there to burn off surplus, especially in longer trips. Allocations with inputs produce nothing until every input it needs is in stock.
nomad_manual.man_mining: Most raw inputs come from a mining allocation. Wait within range of a fully surveyed body and the Flotilla mines on its own, faster where the deposit is richer. Each resource the body has is mined at the full rate, so a body with more resource types mines more. Mining does nothing in hyperspace or over an unsurveyed body.
nomad_manual.man_storage: Everything the Flotilla stores shares one pool, the Space left over after Works and allocations. All goods held together cannot exceed the pool, and each good fills only to the smaller of the room left and a Maximum you set for it. Allocating Space or building Works shrinks the pool. If it shrinks below what is already held, the goods that no longer fit are discarded. Lowering a good's Maximum below what you hold does the same to the excess. Neither is moved to your cargo.
nomad_manual.man_autoforge: The autoforge builds ships and weapons in the background, one at a time. Each job needs production points equal to the value of what it builds. While the queue is not empty, the allocation turns stored Metals, Transplutonics, and Heavy Machinery into points, and the points apply to the job at the front until it is complete. Queued jobs begin once their previous job finishes More autoforges produce points faster, but the overall cost of the product is unchanged. Queuing a job takes no materials. The consumption begins only once something is in the queue.
